items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: If everybody can appreciate what Michael Jordan does

ctx.x: Oh, I agree. And I feel that way about students a lot of times. And we’ve talked about it. Well you know this guy’s not going to be a great player — why waste time with a student that’s not very — I say well, you’re making somebody that’s going to go out, if nothing else, he’s going to be able to appreciate somebody that can do it, and go buy a CD. We’re

all amateur athletes, and that’s why sports demands so much money. But we’re not amateur artists and we’re not amateurs in this country. We’re not amateur artists, we’re not amateur musicians. And that’s why the arts is in such bad shape. If everybody can appreciate what Michael Jordan does, because everybody’s tried to shoot a basket at some time or another. But nobody’s tried, it’s not taught in schools anymore — music is not taught in elementary school like it was. And so people don’t appreciate what Harry…
Lot of food for thought there. Speaking of food—
